assert master["CELLNAME"].nunique() == 59

master["drug_A"] = pd.to_numeric(
    master["drug_A"], errors="raise"
).astype(np.int32)

master["drug_B"] = pd.to_numeric(
    master["drug_B"], errors="raise"
).astype(np.int32)

print("MASTER:", master.shape)
print("Drugs:", len(set(master["drug_A"]) | set(master["drug_B"])))
print("Cells:", master["CELLNAME"].nunique())

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# LOAD EXISTING NSC -> INTERNAL ID MAPPING
# ------------------------------------------------------------

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("LOADING EXISTING DRUG ID MAPPING")
print("=" * 70)

drug_map = pd.read_csv(DRUG_MAP_PATH)

drug_map["NSC"] = pd.to_numeric(
    drug_map["NSC"], errors="raise"
).astype(np.int32)

drug_map["drug_id"] = pd.to_numeric(
    drug_map["drug_id"], errors="raise"
).astype(np.int32)

assert drug_map["NSC"].nunique() == 104
assert drug_map["drug_id"].nunique() == 104

nsc_to_id = (
    drug_map
    .drop_duplicates("NSC")
    .set_index("NSC")["drug_id"]
    .to_dict()
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# MAP MASTER NSC -> INTERNAL DRUG ID
# ------------------------------------------------------------

master["drug_A_id"] = master["drug_A"].map(nsc_to_id)
master["drug_B_id"] = master["drug_B"].map(nsc_to_id)

assert master["drug_A_id"].notna().all()
assert master["drug_B_id"].notna().all()

master["drug_A_id"] = master["drug_A_id"].astype(np.int16)
master["drug_B_id"] = master["drug_B_id"].astype(np.int16)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CANONICAL PAIR KEY
# ------------------------------------------------------------

master["PAIR_KEY"] = (
    master[["drug_A_id", "drug_B_id"]]
    .min(axis=1)
    .astype(str)
    + "_"
    +
    master[["drug_A_id", "drug_B_id"]]
    .max(axis=1)
    .astype(str)
)

print("Unique MASTER drug pairs:", master["PAIR_KEY"].nunique())

assert master["PAIR_KEY"].nunique() == 5143

print("PASS — MASTER contains exactly 5,143 unique drug pairs")

# ============================================================
# CELLMINER — USE EXISTING PCA OUTPUT
# ============================================================
#
# If `cellminer_pca` already exists from the previous successful
# cell, we reuse it.
#
# Otherwise, create it here WITHOUT creating a giant matrix.
# PCA is used only as a compact representation for this
# preliminary CatBoost feature-validation stage.
# ============================================================

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("CELLMINER")
print("=" * 70)

if "cellminer_pca" in globals():

    print("Reusing existing CellMiner PCA object.")

    cellminer_pca = cellminer_pca.copy()

else:

    from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
    from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
    from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

    cellminer = pd.read_csv(CELLMINER_PATH)

    assert cellminer.shape[0] == 59
    assert cellminer.columns[0] == "CELLNAME"
    assert cellminer["CELLNAME"].nunique() == 59

    master_cells = set(master["CELLNAME"])
    cellminer_cells = set(cellminer["CELLNAME"])

    assert master_cells == cellminer_cells

    cell_features = cellminer.drop(columns=["CELLNAME"]).apply(
        pd.to_numeric,
        errors="raise"
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # IMPUTE CNV MISSINGNESS
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    imputer = SimpleImputer(strategy="median")

    X = imputer.fit_transform(cell_features)

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # STANDARDIZE
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    scaler = StandardScaler()

    X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # PCA
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    pca = PCA(
        n_components=0.95,
        svd_solver="full",
        random_state=42
    )

    X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)

    pca_columns = [
        f"CELL_PC_{i+1}"
        for i in range(X_pca.shape[1])
    ]

    cellminer_pca = pd.DataFrame(
        X_pca,
        columns=pca_columns
    )

    cellminer_pca.insert(
        0,
        "CELLNAME",
        cellminer["CELLNAME"].values
    )

    del cellminer, cell_features, X, X_scaled, X_pca
    gc.collect()

print("CellMiner PCA shape:", cellminer_pca.shape)
print(
    "Variance explained:",
    round(
        (
            pca.explained_variance_ratio_.sum()
            if "pca" in globals()
            else np.nan
        ),
        4
    )
)

assert cellminer_pca["CELLNAME"].nunique() == 59

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# ATTACH CELL PCs TO MASTER
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cell_pc_columns = [
    c for c in cellminer_pca.columns
    if c != "CELLNAME"
]

master = master.merge(
    cellminer_pca,
    on="CELLNAME",
    how="left",
    validate="many_to_one"
)

assert len(master) == 294073
assert master[cell_pc_columns].isna().sum().sum() == 0

print(
    "MASTER after CellMiner:",
    master.shape
)

print(
    "CellMiner PCs:",
    len(cell_pc_columns)
)

# Free PCA table
del cellminer_pca
gc.collect()

# ============================================================
# FUNCTION: PREPARE PAIR FEATURE TABLE
# ============================================================

def prepare_pair_features(df, name):

    print("\n" + "-" * 70)
    print(name)
    print("-" * 70)

    df = df.copy()

    assert "PAIR_KEY" in df.columns, (
        f"{name}: PAIR_KEY missing."
    )

    # Remove identifier columns that are not model features.
    identifier_cols = [
        c for c in df.columns
        if c in [
            "drug_A",
            "drug_B",
            "drug_A_id",
            "drug_B_id",
            "Drug_A_Name",
            "Drug_B_Name",
            "PAIR_KEY"
        ]
    ]

    feature_cols = [
        c for c in df.columns
        if c not in identifier_cols
    ]

    # Keep numeric model features only.
    non_numeric = [
        c for c in feature_cols
        if not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[c])
    ]

    assert len(non_numeric) == 0, (
        f"{name}: non-numeric feature columns: {non_numeric}"
    )

    # One row per pair.
    assert not df["PAIR_KEY"].duplicated().any(), (
        f"{name}: duplicate PAIR_KEY values."
    )

    # Exact pair universe.
    master_pairs = set(master["PAIR_KEY"])
    feature_pairs = set(df["PAIR_KEY"])

    missing = master_pairs - feature_pairs
    extra = feature_pairs - master_pairs

    print("Rows:", len(df))
    print("Features:", len(feature_cols))
    print("Missing MASTER pairs:", len(missing))
    print("Extra pairs:", len(extra))

    assert len(missing) == 0, (
        f"{name}: missing MASTER pairs."
    )

    assert len(extra) == 0, (
        f"{name}: extra pairs."
    )

    return df[["PAIR_KEY"] + feature_cols], feature_cols

# ============================================================
# FIX PAIR KEY HANDLING
# ============================================================
# STRING uses MASTER NSC identifiers directly.
# KEGG / STRUCTURE / SIMILARITY / TARGET use internal drug_id.
# ============================================================

def make_pair_key(a, b):
    a = pd.to_numeric(a, errors="raise").astype(np.int32)
    b = pd.to_numeric(b, errors="raise").astype(np.int32)

    lo = np.minimum(a, b)
    hi = np.maximum(a, b)

    return lo.astype(str) + "_" + hi.astype(str)

if "PAIR_KEY" not in string_pair.columns:

    def make_pair_key(a, b):

        b = int(b)
        return f"{min(a,b)}_{max(a,b)}"

    string_pair["PAIR_KEY"] = [
        make_pair_key(a, b)
        for a, b in zip(
            string_pair["drug_A"],
            string_pair["drug_B"]
        )
    ]

      string_pair["PAIR_KEY"].nunique())

      string_pair["PAIR_KEY"].duplicated().sum())

# ------------------------------------------------------------

    c for c in string_pair.columns
    if c not in [
        "drug_A",
        "drug_B",
        "PAIR_KEY"
    ]
]

print("\nSTRING feature columns:")
print(string_feature_cols)

# 4. Check whether repeated rows have consistent features
# ------------------------------------------------------------

print("\nChecking repeated STRING pair values...")

for col in string_feature_cols:

    nunique_per_pair = (
        string_pair
        .groupby("PAIR_KEY")[col]
        .nunique(dropna=False)
    )

    inconsistent = (nunique_per_pair > 1).sum()

    print(
        f"{col}: inconsistent pairs = {inconsistent}"
    )

    assert inconsistent == 0, (
        f"STRING feature '{col}' has different values "
        f"for the same drug pair."
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------

string_pair_reduced = (

# ============================================================
# TRUSTSYN — FINAL DRUG PAIR ALIGNMENT
# ============================================================
# This cell fixes the PAIR_KEY issue and aligns all pair-level
# drug features to the frozen MASTER pair universe.
#
# IMPORTANT:
# - MASTER drug_A/drug_B are NSC IDs
# - KEGG / STRUCTURE / SIMILARITY / TARGET use internal drug_id
# - Do NOT directly compare NSC IDs to internal IDs
# - Do NOT create the giant 294k x 48k matrix here
# ============================================================

import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

print("=" * 70)
print("TRUSTSYN — FINAL DRUG PAIR ALIGNMENT")
print("=" * 70)


# ============================================================
# 1. ROBUST SCALAR PAIR KEY
# ============================================================

def make_pair_key(a, b):
    """
    Canonical unordered pair key.

    Works on scalar Python ints/floats/strings.
    Does NOT use .astype() on scalars.
    """
    a = int(float(a))
    b = int(float(b))

    lo = min(a, b)
    hi = max(a, b)

    return f"{lo}__{hi}"

# ============================================================
# 6. HELPER — ADD NSC PAIR KEY TO STRING
# ============================================================

def prepare_string(df):

    df = df.copy()

    assert {"drug_A", "drug_B"}.issubset(df.columns)

    df["drug_A"] = pd.to_numeric(
        df["drug_A"], errors="raise"
    ).astype(int)

    df["drug_B"] = pd.to_numeric(
        df["drug_B"], errors="raise"
    ).astype(int)

    df["PAIR_KEY"] = [
        make_pair_key(a, b)
        for a, b in zip(
            df["drug_A"],
            df["drug_B"]
        )
    ]

    return df


# ============================================================
# 7. HELPER — ADD INTERNAL PAIR KEY
# ============================================================

def prepare_internal_pair(df, name):

    df = df.copy()

    assert {"drug_A_id", "drug_B_id"}.issubset(df.columns), (
        f"{name}: internal drug ID columns missing."
    )

    df["drug_A_id"] = pd.to_numeric(
        df["drug_A_id"], errors="raise"
    ).astype(int)

    df["drug_B_id"] = pd.to_numeric(
        df["drug_B_id"], errors="raise"
    ).astype(int)

    df["INTERNAL_PAIR_KEY"] = [
        make_pair_key(a, b)
        for a, b in zip(
            df["drug_A_id"],
            df["drug_B_id"]
        )
    ]

    return df

def validate_internal_feature(
    df,
    name,
    feature_key="INTERNAL_PAIR_KEY"
):

    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print(name)
    print("=" * 70)

    print("Rows:", len(df))
    print(
        "Unique internal pairs:",
        df[feature_key].nunique()
    )

    duplicates = df[feature_key].duplicated().sum()

    print("Duplicate pair keys:", duplicates)

    assert duplicates == 0, (
        f"{name}: duplicate internal pair keys."
    )

    master_keys = set(
        master_pairs["INTERNAL_PAIR_KEY"]
    )

    feature_keys = set(
        df[feature_key]
    )

    missing = master_keys - feature_keys
    extra = feature_keys - master_keys

    print("Missing:", len(missing))
    print("Extra:", len(extra))

    if len(missing) > 0:
        print(
            "First missing:",
            list(sorted(missing))[:10]
        )

    if len(extra) > 0:
        print(
            "First extra:",
            list(sorted(extra))[:10]
        )

    assert len(missing) == 0, (
        f"{name}: missing MASTER pairs."
    )

    assert len(extra) == 0, (
        f"{name}: extra pairs not in MASTER."
    )

    print(
        f"PASS — {name} exactly matches MASTER pair universe"
    )

# STRING DUPLICATE DIAGNOSTIC + SAFE COLLAPSE

print("=" * 70)
print("STRING DUPLICATE PAIR DIAGNOSTIC")
print("=" * 70)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Confirm duplicate structure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

dup_mask = string_pair["PAIR_KEY"].duplicated(keep=False)

string_dups = (
    string_pair.loc[dup_mask]
    .sort_values("PAIR_KEY")
    .copy()
)

print("Total STRING rows:", len(string_pair))
print("Unique PAIR_KEYs:", string_pair["PAIR_KEY"].nunique())
print("Rows involved in duplicates:", len(string_dups))
print(
    "Number of duplicated PAIR_KEYs:",
    string_dups["PAIR_KEY"].nunique()
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Show exactly what is duplicated
# ------------------------------------------------------------

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("FIRST DUPLICATED PAIRS")
print("=" * 70)

display(
    string_dups.head(30)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Check whether duplicated rows have conflicting
#    feature values
# ------------------------------------------------------------

feature_cols = [
    c for c in string_pair.columns
    if c not in ["drug_A", "drug_B", "PAIR_KEY"]
]

print("\nSTRING feature columns:")
print(feature_cols)

conflicting_pairs = []

for key, group in string_dups.groupby("PAIR_KEY", sort=False):

    conflict = False

    for col in feature_cols:

        if group[col].nunique(dropna=False) > 1:
            conflict = True
            break

    if conflict:
        conflicting_pairs.append(key)

print("\nDuplicated pairs with conflicting feature values:",
      len(conflicting_pairs))

if conflicting_pairs:
    print(
        "First conflicting pairs:",
        conflicting_pairs[:20]
    )

    display(
        string_dups[
            string_dups["PAIR_KEY"].isin(
                conflicting_pairs[:10]
            )
        ]
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Check whether duplicates are exact duplicates
# ------------------------------------------------------------

duplicate_rows_exact = (
    string_pair.duplicated(
        subset=["PAIR_KEY"] + feature_cols,
        keep=False
    ).sum()
)

print("\nExact duplicate rows:", duplicate_rows_exact)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. IMPORTANT DECISION
# ------------------------------------------------------------

if len(conflicting_pairs) > 0:

    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("STOP — STRING HAS CONFLICTING VALUES")
    print("=" * 70)

    print(
        "We will NOT arbitrarily collapse these rows."
    )

    print(
        "The duplicated PAIR_KEYs contain different "
        "STRING feature values."
    )

    print(
        "This needs to be resolved from the source structure."
    )

else:

    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("STRING DUPLICATES ARE NON-CONFLICTING")
    print("=" * 70)

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Safe collapse:
    # keep one representation of each pair
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    string_pair_clean = (
        string_pair
        .drop_duplicates(
            subset=["PAIR_KEY"],
            keep="first"
        )
        .copy()
    )

    print(
        "STRING rows before:",
        len(string_pair)
    )

    print(
        "STRING rows after:",
        len(string_pair_clean)
    )

    print(
        "STRING unique pairs:",
        string_pair_clean["PAIR_KEY"].nunique()
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Compare against MASTER
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    master_string_keys = set(
        master_pairs["PAIR_KEY"]
    )

    string_keys = set(
        string_pair_clean["PAIR_KEY"]
    )

    string_missing = (
        master_string_keys - string_keys
    )

    string_extra = (
        string_keys - master_string_keys
    )

    print("\nMissing MASTER pairs:", len(string_missing))
    print("Extra STRING pairs:", len(string_extra))

    if len(string_missing) > 0:
        print(
            "First missing:",
            sorted(string_missing)[:20]
        )

    if len(string_extra) > 0:
        print(
            "First extra:",
            sorted(string_extra)[:20]
        )

    assert len(string_missing) == 0, (
        "STRING is missing MASTER pairs."
    )

    assert len(string_extra) == 0, (
        "STRING contains extra pairs."
    )

    print("\nPASS — STRING now has exactly one row per MASTER pair")

# ============================================================
# TRUSTSYN — RECREATE CELLMINER PCA AFTER KERNEL RESTART
# ============================================================

import os
import gc
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

print("=" * 70)
print("RECREATING CELLMINER PCA")
print("=" * 70)


# ============================================================
# 1. PATHS — THESE ARE THE ACTUAL VALIDATED FILES
# ============================================================

CELLMINER_PATH = (
    "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/data/Generated_features/"
    "cellminer_features/cellminer_all_features_59cell.csv"
)

MASTER_PATH = (
    "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/data/processed/almanac/"
    "almanac_final_59cell_104drug.csv"
)


# ============================================================
# 2. LOAD ONLY THE VALIDATED CELLMINER TABLE
# ============================================================

assert os.path.exists(CELLMINER_PATH), (
    f"CellMiner file not found:\n{CELLMINER_PATH}"
)

cellminer_pca_source = pd.read_csv(
    CELLMINER_PATH
)

print(
    "Loaded CellMiner:",
    cellminer_pca_source.shape
)

assert cellminer_pca_source.shape == (59, 48886)

assert (
    cellminer_pca_source.columns[0]
    == "CELLNAME"
)

assert (
    cellminer_pca_source["CELLNAME"].nunique()
    == 59
)

assert (
    cellminer_pca_source["CELLNAME"].duplicated().sum()
    == 0
)

print("PASS — validated 59-cell CellMiner table")


# ============================================================
# 3. IDENTIFY FEATURES
# ============================================================

cell_col = "CELLNAME"

cellminer_feature_cols = [
    c
    for c in cellminer_pca_source.columns
    if c != cell_col
]

print(
    "Input CellMiner features:",
    len(cellminer_feature_cols)
)

assert len(cellminer_feature_cols) == 48885


# ============================================================
# 4. CHECK DATA
# ============================================================

X_cellminer = cellminer_pca_source[
    cellminer_feature_cols
].to_numpy(
    dtype=np.float32
)

print(
    "Raw CellMiner matrix:",
    X_cellminer.shape
)

assert X_cellminer.shape == (59, 48885)

assert np.isfinite(X_cellminer).all()

print("PASS — no NaN/infinite values")


# ============================================================
# 5. STANDARDIZE BEFORE PCA
# ============================================================

print("\nStandardizing CellMiner features...")

scaler = StandardScaler()

X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(
    X_cellminer
).astype(
    np.float32,
    copy=False
)

print(
    "Scaled matrix:",
    X_scaled.shape
)


# ============================================================
# 6. PCA — 50 COMPONENTS
# ============================================================

print("\nRunning PCA...")

pca = PCA(
    n_components=50,
    random_state=42
)

X_pca = pca.fit_transform(
    X_scaled
).astype(
    np.float32,
    copy=False
)

variance_explained = (
    pca.explained_variance_ratio_.sum()
)

print(
    "PCA output:",
    X_pca.shape
)

print(
    "Variance explained:",
    round(
        variance_explained,
        4
    )
)

assert X_pca.shape == (59, 50)

print(
    "PASS — CellMiner compressed to 50 components"
)


# ============================================================
# 7. BUILD PCA TABLE
# ============================================================

pca_columns = [
    f"CellMiner_PC{i}"
    for i in range(1, 51)
]

cellminer_pca = pd.DataFrame(
    X_pca,
    columns=pca_columns
)

cellminer_pca.insert(
    0,
    "CELLNAME",
    cellminer_pca_source[
        "CELLNAME"
    ].values
)


# ============================================================
# 8. FINAL PCA VALIDATION
# ============================================================

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("CELLMINER PCA OBJECT READY")
print("=" * 70)

print(
    "Shape:",
    cellminer_pca.shape
)

print(
    "Cells:",
    cellminer_pca["CELLNAME"].nunique()
)

print(
    "Components:",
    len(pca_columns)
)

print(
    "Variance explained:",
    round(
        variance_explained,
        4
    )
)

assert cellminer_pca.shape == (59, 51)
assert cellminer_pca["CELLNAME"].nunique() == 59
assert cellminer_pca["CELLNAME"].duplicated().sum() == 0
assert cellminer_pca[pca_columns].isna().sum().sum() == 0
assert np.isfinite(
    cellminer_pca[pca_columns].to_numpy()
).all()


# ============================================================
# 9. FREE THE LARGE CELLMINER MATRICES
# ============================================================

del X_cellminer
del X_scaled
del X_pca
del cellminer_pca_source

gc.collect()


# ============================================================
# 10. FINAL CHECK
# ============================================================

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("PASS — CELLMINER PCA RECREATED")
print("=" * 70)

print(
    "cellminer_pca:",
    cellminer_pca.shape
)

print(
    "Raw CellMiner matrix released from memory."
)

print(
    "Ready to continue with the 294,073-row merge."
)

import os

from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

)

).astype(

# ============================================================
# 5. HELPER — FIND SPLIT FILES
# ============================================================

def find_split_files(directory):

    if not os.path.exists(directory):
        return []

    valid_extensions = (
        ".csv",
        ".parquet",
        ".pkl",
        ".pickle",
        ".npy",
        ".npz",
    )

    return sorted([
        os.path.join(directory, f)
        for f in os.listdir(directory)
        if f.lower().endswith(valid_extensions)
    ])


# ============================================================
# 6. LOAD SPLIT OBJECTS
# ============================================================

def load_split_file(path):

    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()

    if ext == ".csv":
        return pd.read_csv(path)

    elif ext == ".parquet":
        return pd.read_parquet(path)

    elif ext in [".pkl", ".pickle"]:
        return pd.read_pickle(path)

    elif ext == ".npy":
        return np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)

    elif ext == ".npz":
        return np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)

    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported split file: {path}")


# ============================================================
# 7. INSPECT SPLITS
# ============================================================

all_split_files = {}

for split_name, directory in SPLIT_DIRS.items():

    files = find_split_files(directory)

    all_split_files[split_name] = files

    print("\n" + "-" * 70)
    print(split_name.upper())

    if len(files) == 0:
        print("No split files found.")

    else:
        for f in files:
            print(os.path.basename(f))


# ============================================================
# 8. IMPORTANT:
#    DO NOT GUESS THE SPLIT FORMAT
# ============================================================

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("SPLIT FILE INSPECTION")
print("=" * 70)

for split_name, files in all_split_files.items():

    for f in files:

        print("\n" + "-" * 70)
        print(split_name, "->", os.path.basename(f))

        try:

            obj = load_split_file(f)

            print("Type:", type(obj))

            if isinstance(obj, pd.DataFrame):

                print("Shape:", obj.shape)
                print("Columns:", list(obj.columns))

            elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):

                print("Shape:", obj.shape)
                print("dtype:", obj.dtype)

            elif isinstance(obj, dict):

                print("Keys:", list(obj.keys()))

        except Exception as e:

            print("Could not inspect:", repr(e))

# ============================================================
# TRUSTSYN — INSPECT EXISTING SPLITS
# ============================================================

import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

SPLIT_DIRS = {
    "random": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/random",
    "cold_combination": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_combination",
    "cold_cell": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_cell",
    "cold_drug": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_drug",
}

print("=" * 70)
print("EXISTING TRUSTSYN SPLITS")
print("=" * 70)

for split_name, directory in SPLIT_DIRS.items():

    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print(split_name.upper())
    print(directory)
    print("=" * 70)

    if not os.path.exists(directory):
        print("DIRECTORY NOT FOUND")
        continue

    files = sorted(os.listdir(directory))

    if not files:
        print("EMPTY DIRECTORY")
        continue

    for filename in files:

        path = os.path.join(directory, filename)

        if os.path.isdir(path):
            print("[DIR] ", filename)
            continue

        print("\nFILE:", filename)

        try:

            if filename.endswith(".csv"):

                df = pd.read_csv(path)

                print("Type: DataFrame")
                print("Shape:", df.shape)
                print("Columns:", df.columns.tolist())

                print("\nFirst 3 rows:")
                print(df.head(3).to_string(index=False))

            elif filename.endswith(".parquet"):

                df = pd.read_parquet(path)

                print("Type: DataFrame")
                print("Shape:", df.shape)
                print("Columns:", df.columns.tolist())

            elif filename.endswith(".npy"):

                arr = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)

                print("Type: ndarray")
                print("Shape:", arr.shape)
                print("dtype:", arr.dtype)

            elif filename.endswith(".npz"):

                arr = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)

                print("Type: npz")
                print("Keys:", arr.files)

                for key in arr.files:
                    print(
                        " ",
                        key,
                        "shape=",
                        arr[key].shape
                    )

            elif filename.endswith((".pkl", ".pickle")):

                obj = pd.read_pickle(path)

                print("Type:", type(obj))

                if isinstance(obj, pd.DataFrame):
                    print("Shape:", obj.shape)
                    print("Columns:", obj.columns.tolist())

                elif isinstance(obj, dict):
                    print("Keys:", list(obj.keys()))

            else:
                print("Skipped non-data file")

        except Exception as e:

            print(
                "ERROR READING FILE:",
                repr(e)
            )


print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("SPLIT INSPECTION COMPLETE")
print("=" * 70)

import os

from catboost import CatBoostRegressor

    mean_squared_error,

    r2_score
)

# ============================================================
# 1. CHECK EXISTING MODEL OBJECTS
# ============================================================

print("=" * 70)
print("CHECKING MODEL OBJECTS")
print("=" * 70)

assert "MASTER_MODEL" in globals()
assert "X" in globals()

assert np.isfinite(y).all()

print("X:", X.shape)

print("PASS — model objects valid")


# ============================================================
# 2. DEFINE THE EXACT MASTER ROW IDENTIFIER
# ============================================================
#
# The split CSVs do not contain the original DataFrame index.
# Therefore we reconstruct row identity using all MASTER
# columns that define an observation.
#
# This avoids relying on row order.
# ============================================================

ROW_COLS = [
    "drug_A",
    "drug_B",
    "CELLNAME",
    "tissue",
    "combo_score",
    "CONC1",
    "CONC2",
    "cellminer_cellline_id",
    "nci_almanac_cellname"
]

assert all(c in MASTER_MODEL.columns for c in ROW_COLS)

print("\nCreating MASTER row hashes...")

master_hash = pd.util.hash_pandas_object(
    MASTER_MODEL[ROW_COLS],
    index=False
).to_numpy()

assert len(master_hash) == len(MASTER_MODEL)
assert len(np.unique(master_hash)) == len(master_hash)

print("Unique MASTER row hashes:", len(np.unique(master_hash)))
print("PASS — MASTER rows uniquely identifiable")


# ============================================================
# 3. CREATE HASH -> MASTER POSITION LOOKUP
# ============================================================

master_hash_to_position = {
    h: i
    for i, h in enumerate(master_hash)
}

print("MASTER lookup created")


# ============================================================
# 4. FUNCTION TO LOAD A SPLIT
# ============================================================

def load_split(split_path, split_name):

    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print(f"LOADING {split_name.upper()} SPLIT")
    print("=" * 70)

    df = pd.read_csv(split_path)

    print("Rows:", len(df))

    assert all(c in df.columns for c in ROW_COLS), (
        f"{split_name}: required columns missing"
    )

    # Generate exactly the same row hash
    split_hash = pd.util.hash_pandas_object(
        df[ROW_COLS],
        index=False
    ).to_numpy()

    # Verify every split row exists in MASTER
    missing = np.sum(
        ~np.isin(split_hash, master_hash)
    )

    print("Rows missing from MASTER:", missing)

    assert missing == 0, (
        f"{split_name}: rows not found in MASTER"
    )

    # Convert hashes to MASTER positions
    positions = np.array(
        [master_hash_to_position[h] for h in split_hash],
        dtype=np.int64
    )

    # Verify one-to-one correspondence
    assert len(positions) == len(df)
    assert len(np.unique(positions)) == len(df)

    print("Mapped MASTER rows:", len(positions))
    print("Unique MASTER rows:", len(np.unique(positions)))
    print("PASS — split mapped exactly to MASTER")

    return df, positions

def check_split_disjointness(train_idx, val_idx, test_idx, name):

    train_set = set(train_idx)
    val_set = set(val_idx)
    test_set = set(test_idx)

    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print(f"{name.upper()} SPLIT DISJOINTNESS")
    print("=" * 70)

    print("Train:", len(train_set))
    print("Val  :", len(val_set))
    print("Test :", len(test_set))

    assert train_set.isdisjoint(val_set)
    assert train_set.isdisjoint(test_set)
    assert val_set.isdisjoint(test_set)

    print("PASS — train/validation/test are disjoint")

def check_full_coverage(train_idx, val_idx, test_idx, name):

    combined = np.concatenate([
        train_idx,

        test_idx
    ])

    unique_combined = np.unique(combined)

    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print(f"{name.upper()} COVERAGE")
    print("=" * 70)

    print("Combined rows:", len(combined))
    print("Unique rows:", len(unique_combined))

    assert len(combined) == len(unique_combined)

    print("PASS — no duplicated rows across splits")

# ============================================================
# 10. CATBOOST EVALUATION FUNCTION
# ============================================================

def evaluate_catboost_split(
    name,
    train_idx,
    val_idx,
    test_idx
):

    print("\n\n" + "=" * 70)
    print(f"CATBOOST — {name.upper()}")
    print("=" * 70)

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Extract only required rows from the existing X/y matrix
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    X_train = X[train_idx]
    X_val   = X[val_idx]
    X_test  = X[test_idx]

    y_train = y[train_idx]
    y_val   = y[val_idx]
    y_test  = y[test_idx]

    print("X_train:", X_train.shape)
    print("X_val  :", X_val.shape)
    print("X_test :", X_test.shape)

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # CatBoost baseline
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    model = CatBoostRegressor(
        loss_function="RMSE",
        eval_metric="RMSE",

        iterations=1000,
        learning_rate=0.05,
        depth=8,

        l2_leaf_reg=5,
        random_seed=42,

        verbose=100,
        allow_writing_files=False
    )

    print("\nTraining CatBoost...")

    model.fit(
        X_train,
        y_train,
        eval_set=(X_val, y_val),
        use_best_model=True,
        early_stopping_rounds=100
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Predictions
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print("\nGenerating predictions...")

    pred_val = model.predict(X_val)
    pred_test = model.predict(X_test)

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Metrics
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    def metrics(y_true, pred):

        rmse = np.sqrt(
            mean_squared_error(y_true, pred)
        )

        mae = mean_absolute_error(
            y_true,
            pred
        )

        r2 = r2_score(
            y_true,
            pred
        )

        pearson = pearsonr(
            y_true,
            pred
        )[0]

        spearman = spearmanr(
            y_true,
            pred
        ).statistic

        return {
            "RMSE": rmse,
            "MAE": mae,
            "Pearson": pearson,
            "Spearman": spearman,
            "R2": r2
        }

    val_metrics = metrics(
        y_val,
        pred_val
    )

    test_metrics = metrics(
        y_test,
        pred_test
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Print
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print("\n" + "-" * 70)
    print("BEST ITERATION")
    print("-" * 70)

    print(model.get_best_iteration())

    print("\n" + "-" * 70)
    print("VALIDATION METRICS")
    print("-" * 70)

    for k, v in val_metrics.items():
        print(f"{k:10s}: {v:.6f}")

    print("\n" + "-" * 70)
    print("TEST METRICS")
    print("-" * 70)

    for k, v in test_metrics.items():
        print(f"{k:10s}: {v:.6f}")

    print("\nPASS — CatBoost completed")

    return {
        "model": model,
        "val_metrics": val_metrics,
        "test_metrics": test_metrics,
        "pred_val": pred_val,
        "pred_test": pred_test
    }


# ============================================================
# 11. RUN RANDOM CATBOOST
# ============================================================

random_results = evaluate_catboost_split(
    "random",
    random_train_idx,
    random_val_idx,
    random_test_idx
)

gc.collect()


# ============================================================

    cc_test_idx

import os
import pandas as pd

CANDIDATE_DIRS = [
    "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/notebooks/splits/cold_cell",
    "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_cell_line",
]

for directory in CANDIDATE_DIRS:

    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("DIRECTORY")
    print(directory)
    print("=" * 80)

    if not os.path.isdir(directory):
        print("DIRECTORY NOT FOUND")
        continue

    files = sorted(os.listdir(directory))

    print("Files:", files)

    for filename in files:

        if not filename.lower().endswith(".csv"):
            print(f"\nSkipping non-CSV: {filename}")
            continue

        path = os.path.join(directory, filename)

        try:
            df = pd.read_csv(path)

            print("\n" + "-" * 70)
            print("FILE:", filename)
            print("Shape:", df.shape)
            print("Columns:", list(df.columns))

            if "CELLNAME" in df.columns:

                print(
                    "Unique cells:",
                    df["CELLNAME"].nunique()
                )

                print(
                    "Cells:",
                    sorted(df["CELLNAME"].dropna().unique())
                )

                print(
                    "Duplicate rows:",
                    df.duplicated().sum()
                )

                print(
                    "Rows:",
                    len(df)
                )

        except Exception as e:

            print(
                f"\nCould not read {filename}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
            )

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("COLD CELL CANDIDATE INSPECTION COMPLETE")
print("=" * 80)

assert cold_cell_test["CELLNAME"].nunique() == 6

) == 59

print("\nPASS — Cold Cell has no cell leakage")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CREATE ROW-LEVEL KEYS
#
# IMPORTANT:

# This avoids relying on DataFrame ordering.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

KEY_COLS = [
    "drug_A",
    "drug_B",
    "CELLNAME",
    "tissue",
    "combo_score",
    "CONC1",
    "CONC2",
    "cellminer_cellline_id",
    "nci_almanac_cellname",

assert len(MASTER_MODEL) == 294073
assert len(X) == 294073
assert len(y) == 294073

master_keys = MASTER_MODEL[KEY_COLS].copy()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# BUILD UNIQUE ROW IDENTIFIER
# ------------------------------------------------------------

def make_row_key(df):

    return (
        df[KEY_COLS]
        .astype(str)
        .fillna("<NA>")
        .agg("||".join, axis=1)
    )

master_row_keys = make_row_key(master_keys)

assert master_row_keys.nunique() == 294073

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# MAP EACH SPLIT TO MASTER ROWS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

def get_split_indices(split_df, name):

    split_keys = make_row_key(split_df)

    assert split_keys.nunique() == len(split_df), (
        f"{name} contains duplicate row keys."
    )

    master_index = pd.Series(
        np.arange(len(MASTER_MODEL)),
        index=master_row_keys
    )

    missing = split_keys[
        ~split_keys.isin(master_index.index)
    ]

    assert len(missing) == 0, (
        f"{name}: {len(missing)} rows not found in MASTER_MODEL."
    )

    indices = master_index.loc[
        split_keys
    ].to_numpy()

    assert len(indices) == len(split_df)

    assert len(np.unique(indices)) == len(indices), (
        f"{name}: duplicate MASTER indices."
    )

    return indices


cold_cell_train_idx = get_split_indices(
    cold_cell_train,
    "Cold Cell TRAIN"
)

cold_cell_val_idx = get_split_indices(
    cold_cell_val,
    "Cold Cell VAL"
)

cold_cell_test_idx = get_split_indices(
    cold_cell_test,
    "Cold Cell TEST"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------

    set(cold_cell_train_idx)
    & set(cold_cell_val_idx)
) == 0

) == 0

    & set(cold_cell_test_idx)
) == 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# COMPLETE MASTER COVERAGE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

all_idx = np.concatenate([
    cold_cell_train_idx,
    cold_cell_val_idx,
    cold_cell_test_idx
])

assert len(all_idx) == 294073
assert len(np.unique(all_idx)) == 294073

assert np.array_equal(
    np.sort(all_idx),
    np.arange(294073)
)

print("\n" + "=" * 70)

print("=" * 70)

    "Train indices:",
    len(cold_cell_train_idx)
)

# ================================================================
# TRUSTSYN — VALIDATE ALL EXISTING MODEL SPLITS

# IMPORTANT:

# - Does NOT modify MASTER
# - Only loads and validates

import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

MASTER_PATH = (
    "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/data/processed/almanac/"
    "almanac_final_59cell_104drug.csv"
)

SPLIT_PATHS = {
    "RANDOM": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/random",
    "COLD_COMBINATION": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_combination",
    "COLD_CELL": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_cell_line",
    "COLD_DRUG": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_drug",
}

REQUIRED_COLUMNS = [
    "drug_A",
    "drug_B",
    "CELLNAME",
    "tissue",
    "combo_score",
    "CONC1",
    "CONC2",
    "cellminer_cellline_id",
    "nci_almanac_cellname",
]

EXPECTED_MASTER_ROWS = 294073


# ================================================================
# HELPERS
# ================================================================

def normalize_split(df):
    df = df.copy()

    # Normalize identifiers exactly as MASTER
    df["drug_A"] = pd.to_numeric(df["drug_A"], errors="raise").astype(np.int64)
    df["drug_B"] = pd.to_numeric(df["drug_B"], errors="raise").astype(np.int64)

    df["CELLNAME"] = df["CELLNAME"].astype(str)

    return df


def make_row_key(df):
    """
    Full experimental-row identity.
    This is stronger than checking only drug pairs.
    """
    cols = [
        "drug_A",
        "drug_B",
        "CELLNAME",
        "tissue",
        "combo_score",
        "CONC1",
        "CONC2",
        "cellminer_cellline_id",
        "nci_almanac_cellname",
    ]

    return pd.util.hash_pandas_object(
        df[cols],
        index=False
    )


def make_pair_key(df):
    a = df["drug_A"].to_numpy(dtype=np.int64)
    b = df["drug_B"].to_numpy(dtype=np.int64)

    lo = np.minimum(a, b)
    hi = np.maximum(a, b)

    return pd.Series(
        lo.astype(str) + "_" + hi.astype(str),
        index=df.index
    )


# ================================================================
# LOAD MASTER
# ================================================================

print("=" * 70)
print("LOADING MASTER")
print("=" * 70)

master = pd.read_csv(MASTER_PATH)
master = normalize_split(master)

print("MASTER:", master.shape)
print("Unique drugs:", len(set(master["drug_A"]) | set(master["drug_B"])))
print("Unique cells:", master["CELLNAME"].nunique())

assert master.shape[0] == EXPECTED_MASTER_ROWS
assert master[REQUIRED_COLUMNS].isnull().sum().sum() >= 0

master_row_keys = set(make_row_key(master))

master_pair_keys = set(make_pair_key(master))

print("MASTER unique experimental rows:", len(master_row_keys))
print("MASTER unique drug pairs:", len(master_pair_keys))


# ================================================================
# VALIDATE EACH SPLIT
# ================================================================

results = {}


for split_name, split_dir in SPLIT_PATHS.items():

    print("\n")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(split_name)
    print(split_dir)
    print("=" * 70)

    if not os.path.isdir(split_dir):
        print("DIRECTORY NOT FOUND")
        results[split_name] = {
            "status": "MISSING DIRECTORY"
        }
        continue

    required_files = ["train.csv", "val.csv", "test.csv"]

    missing_files = [
        f for f in required_files
        if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(split_dir, f))
    ]

    if missing_files:
        print("MISSING FILES:", missing_files)

        results[split_name] = {
            "status": "MISSING FILES",
            "missing_files": missing_files
        }
        continue

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # LOAD
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    train = normalize_split(
        pd.read_csv(os.path.join(split_dir, "train.csv"))
    )

    val = normalize_split(
        pd.read_csv(os.path.join(split_dir, "val.csv"))
    )

    test = normalize_split(
        pd.read_csv(os.path.join(split_dir, "test.csv"))
    )

    print("\nShapes:")
    print("Train:", train.shape)
    print("Val  :", val.shape)
    print("Test :", test.shape)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # COLUMN VALIDATION
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    for name, df in [
        ("TRAIN", train),
        ("VAL", val),
        ("TEST", test)
    ]:

        missing_cols = [
            c for c in REQUIRED_COLUMNS
            if c not in df.columns
        ]

        if missing_cols:
            print(f"{name} missing columns:", missing_cols)

        assert not missing_cols, (
            f"{split_name}/{name}: missing required columns"
        )

    print("PASS — required columns present")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # DUPLICATE ROW CHECK
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    train_keys = make_row_key(train)
    val_keys = make_row_key(val)
    test_keys = make_row_key(test)

    train_set = set(train_keys)
    val_set = set(val_keys)
    test_set = set(test_keys)

    train_duplicates = len(train) - len(train_set)
    val_duplicates = len(val) - len(val_set)
    test_duplicates = len(test) - len(test_set)

    print("\nDuplicate rows:")
    print("Train:", train_duplicates)
    print("Val  :", val_duplicates)
    print("Test :", test_duplicates)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # CROSS-SPLIT ROW LEAKAGE
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    train_val_overlap = len(train_set & val_set)
    train_test_overlap = len(train_set & test_set)
    val_test_overlap = len(val_set & test_set)

    print("\nCross-split row overlap:")
    print("Train ∩ Val :", train_val_overlap)
    print("Train ∩ Test:", train_test_overlap)
    print("Val ∩ Test  :", val_test_overlap)

    row_leakage = (
        train_val_overlap
        + train_test_overlap
        + val_test_overlap
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # MASTER COVERAGE
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    combined_set = train_set | val_set | test_set

    missing_from_split = master_row_keys - combined_set
    extra_in_split = combined_set - master_row_keys

    combined_rows = (
        len(train)
        + len(val)
        + len(test)
    )

    print("\nCoverage:")
    print("Combined rows:", combined_rows)
    print("Expected MASTER rows:", EXPECTED_MASTER_ROWS)
    print("Missing MASTER rows:", len(missing_from_split))
    print("Extra rows:", len(extra_in_split))

    exact_partition = (
        combined_rows == EXPECTED_MASTER_ROWS
        and len(missing_from_split) == 0
        and len(extra_in_split) == 0
        and row_leakage == 0
        and train_duplicates == 0
        and val_duplicates == 0
        and test_duplicates == 0
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # CELL LEAKAGE
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    train_cells = set(train["CELLNAME"])
    val_cells = set(val["CELLNAME"])
    test_cells = set(test["CELLNAME"])

    cell_train_val = train_cells & val_cells
    cell_train_test = train_cells & test_cells
    cell_val_test = val_cells & test_cells

    print("\nCell sets:")
    print("Train:", len(train_cells))
    print("Val  :", len(val_cells))
    print("Test :", len(test_cells))

    print("\nCell overlap:")
    print("Train ∩ Val :", len(cell_train_val))
    print("Train ∩ Test:", len(cell_train_test))
    print("Val ∩ Test  :", len(cell_val_test))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # DRUG LEAKAGE
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    train_drugs = set(train["drug_A"]) | set(train["drug_B"])
    val_drugs = set(val["drug_A"]) | set(val["drug_B"])
    test_drugs = set(test["drug_A"]) | set(test["drug_B"])

    drug_train_val = train_drugs & val_drugs
    drug_train_test = train_drugs & test_drugs
    drug_val_test = val_drugs & test_drugs

    print("\nDrug sets:")
    print("Train:", len(train_drugs))
    print("Val  :", len(val_drugs))
    print("Test :", len(test_drugs))

    print("\nDrug overlap:")
    print("Train ∩ Val :", len(drug_train_val))
    print("Train ∩ Test:", len(drug_train_test))
    print("Val ∩ Test  :", len(drug_val_test))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # COMBINATION LEAKAGE
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    train_pairs = set(make_pair_key(train))
    val_pairs = set(make_pair_key(val))
    test_pairs = set(make_pair_key(test))

    pair_train_val = train_pairs & val_pairs
    pair_train_test = train_pairs & test_pairs
    pair_val_test = val_pairs & test_pairs

    print("\nDrug-pair overlap:")
    print("Train ∩ Val :", len(pair_train_val))
    print("Train ∩ Test:", len(pair_train_test))
    print("Val ∩ Test  :", len(pair_val_test))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # SPLIT-SPECIFIC TEST
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    split_specific_pass = True

    if split_name == "COLD_CELL":

        split_specific_pass = (
            len(cell_train_val) == 0
            and len(cell_train_test) == 0
            and len(cell_val_test) == 0
        )

        print("\nCOLD CELL requirement:")
        print(
            "PASS — cell sets are completely disjoint"
            if split_specific_pass
            else "FAIL — cell leakage detected"
        )

    elif split_name == "COLD_DRUG":

        split_specific_pass = (
            len(drug_train_val) == 0
            and len(drug_train_test) == 0
            and len(drug_val_test) == 0
        )

        print("\nCOLD DRUG requirement:")
        print(
            "PASS — drug sets are completely disjoint"
            if split_specific_pass
            else "FAIL — drug leakage detected"
        )

    elif split_name == "COLD_COMBINATION":

        split_specific_pass = (
            len(pair_train_val) == 0
            and len(pair_train_test) == 0
            and len(pair_val_test) == 0
        )

        print("\nCOLD COMBINATION requirement:")
        print(
            "PASS — drug-pair sets are completely disjoint"
            if split_specific_pass
            else "FAIL — combination leakage detected"
        )

    elif split_name == "RANDOM":

        # Random split SHOULD NOT require cells/drugs/pairs
        # to be disjoint. Only row-level separation matters.
        split_specific_pass = row_leakage == 0

        print("\nRANDOM requirement:")
        print(
            "PASS — no row leakage"
            if split_specific_pass
            else "FAIL — row leakage detected"
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # FINAL STATUS
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    overall_pass = (
        exact_partition
        and split_specific_pass
    )

    print("\n" + "-" * 70)

    if overall_pass:
        print(f"PASS — {split_name} IS VALID")
    else:
        print(f"FAIL — {split_name} NEEDS INVESTIGATION")

        if not exact_partition:
            print("Reason: split is NOT an exact partition of current MASTER.")

        if not split_specific_pass:
            print("Reason: split-specific leakage detected.")

    results[split_name] = {
        "status": "PASS" if overall_pass else "FAIL",
        "train_rows": len(train),
        "val_rows": len(val),
        "test_rows": len(test),
        "combined_rows": combined_rows,
        "missing_master_rows": len(missing_from_split),
        "extra_rows": len(extra_in_split),
        "row_leakage": row_leakage,
        "train_cells": len(train_cells),
        "val_cells": len(val_cells),
        "test_cells": len(test_cells),
        "train_drugs": len(train_drugs),
        "val_drugs": len(val_drugs),
        "test_drugs": len(test_drugs),
        "train_pairs": len(train_pairs),
        "val_pairs": len(val_pairs),
        "test_pairs": len(test_pairs),
    }


# ================================================================
# FINAL SUMMARY
# ================================================================

print("\n")
print("=" * 70)
print("FINAL SPLIT VALIDATION SUMMARY")
print("=" * 70)

summary = pd.DataFrame(results).T

print(summary.to_string())

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("IMPORTANT")
print("=" * 70)

print("""
Do NOT train CatBoost yet.

A split is only ready for modeling if:
1. train + val + test exactly cover the current MASTER
2. there are no duplicate rows
3. there is no cross-split row leakage
4. the split-specific leakage rule passes

Random:
    row separation only

Cold Combination:
    drug pairs must be disjoint

Cold Cell:
    cells must be disjoint

Cold Drug:
    drugs must be disjoint
""")

import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

print("=" * 70)
print("COLD DRUG — CURRENT VS OLD SPLIT DIAGNOSTIC")
print("=" * 70)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CURRENT MASTER
# ------------------------------------------------------------
master_drugs = set(
    pd.concat([
        MASTER["drug_A"],
        MASTER["drug_B"]
    ]).astype(int).unique()
)

master_pairs = set(
    zip(
        MASTER["drug_A"].astype(int),
        MASTER["drug_B"].astype(int)
    )
)

print("\nCURRENT MASTER")
print("Rows:", len(MASTER))
print("Unique drugs:", len(master_drugs))
print("Unique pairs:", len(master_pairs))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# OLD COLD DRUG SPLIT
# ------------------------------------------------------------
COLD_DRUG_DIR = "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_drug"

cold_train = pd.read_csv(
    os.path.join(COLD_DRUG_DIR, "train.csv")
)

cold_val = pd.read_csv(
    os.path.join(COLD_DRUG_DIR, "val.csv")
)

cold_test = pd.read_csv(
    os.path.join(COLD_DRUG_DIR, "test.csv")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRUG SETS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
train_drugs = set(
    pd.concat([
        cold_train["drug_A"],
        cold_train["drug_B"]
    ]).astype(int).unique()
)

val_drugs = set(
    pd.concat([
        cold_val["drug_A"],
        cold_val["drug_B"]
    ]).astype(int).unique()
)

test_drugs = set(
    pd.concat([
        cold_test["drug_A"],
        cold_test["drug_B"]
    ]).astype(int).unique()
)

print("\nOLD COLD DRUG DRUG SETS")
print("Train drugs:", len(train_drugs))
print("Val drugs:", len(val_drugs))
print("Test drugs:", len(test_drugs))

print("\nDrug overlaps:")
print("Train ∩ Val :", len(train_drugs & val_drugs))
print("Train ∩ Test:", len(train_drugs & test_drugs))
print("Val ∩ Test  :", len(val_drugs & test_drugs))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# MASTER DRUG COVERAGE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
assigned_drugs = train_drugs | val_drugs | test_drugs

print("\nDRUG COVERAGE")
print("MASTER drugs:", len(master_drugs))
print("Assigned drugs:", len(assigned_drugs))
print("Missing MASTER drugs:", len(master_drugs - assigned_drugs))
print("Extra split drugs:", len(assigned_drugs - master_drugs))

if master_drugs - assigned_drugs:
    print(
        "Missing drug IDs:",
        sorted(master_drugs - assigned_drugs)
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DETERMINE WHERE MASTER PAIRS CAN ACTUALLY GO
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def classify_pair(a, b):
    a = int(a)
    b = int(b)

    if a in train_drugs and b in train_drugs:
        return "TRAIN"

    if a in val_drugs and b in val_drugs:
        return "VAL"

    if a in test_drugs and b in test_drugs:
        return "TEST"

    return "CROSS_GROUP"


master_pair_df = MASTER[
    ["drug_A", "drug_B"]
].drop_duplicates().copy()

master_pair_df["DRUG_SPLIT"] = [
    classify_pair(a, b)
    for a, b in zip(
        master_pair_df["drug_A"],
        master_pair_df["drug_B"]
    )
]

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("MASTER PAIR CLASSIFICATION")
print("=" * 70)

print(
    master_pair_df["DRUG_SPLIT"]
    .value_counts()
    .sort_index()
)

print("\nCross-group MASTER pairs:")
print(
    (master_pair_df["DRUG_SPLIT"] == "CROSS_GROUP").sum()
)

print("\nRows belonging to each legal cold-drug partition:")

for split_name in ["TRAIN", "VAL", "TEST"]:
    pair_set = set(
        zip(
            master_pair_df.loc[
                master_pair_df["DRUG_SPLIT"] == split_name,
                "drug_A"
            ].astype(int),
            master_pair_df.loc[
                master_pair_df["DRUG_SPLIT"] == split_name,
                "drug_B"
            ].astype(int)
        )
    )

    print(split_name, "pairs:", len(pair_set))

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("DIAGNOSTIC COMPLETE")
print("=" * 70)

# ============================================================
# TRUSTSYN — CATBOOST BASELINE ON ALL 4 SPLITS
# ============================================================
#
# Uses ONLY:
#   MASTER_MODEL : (294073, 73)
#   X            : (294073, 64)
#   y            : (294073,)
#
# Existing splits:
#   random
#   cold_combination
#   cold_cell_line
#   cold_drug
#
# NO files are modified.
# NO features are regenerated.
# NO PCA is rerun.
# ============================================================

import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from catboost import CatBoostRegressor
from sklearn.metrics import (
    mean_squared_error,
    mean_absolute_error,
    r2_score
)
from scipy.stats import pearsonr

print("=" * 70)
print("TRUSTSYN — CATBOOST BASELINE")
print("=" * 70)


# ============================================================
# 1. CHECK MODEL OBJECTS
# ============================================================

required_objects = ["MASTER_MODEL", "X", "y"]

for obj in required_objects:
    assert obj in globals(), (
        f"Required object '{obj}' is not in memory."
    )

print("\nMODEL OBJECTS")
print("MASTER_MODEL:", MASTER_MODEL.shape)
print("X:", X.shape)
print("y:", y.shape)

assert MASTER_MODEL.shape == (294073, 73)
assert X.shape == (294073, 64)
assert len(y) == 294073

print("PASS — model objects available")


# ============================================================

X_np = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
y_np = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)

assert X_np.shape == (294073, 64)
assert y_np.shape == (294073,)

assert np.isfinite(X_np).all()
assert np.isfinite(y_np).all()

print("\nPASS — X and y are finite numeric arrays")


# ============================================================
# 3. CREATE A STABLE ROW KEY
# ============================================================
#
# We identify rows using all original MASTER columns.
# This prevents accidental row-order assumptions.
# ============================================================

KEY_COLS = [
    "drug_A",
    "drug_B",
    "CELLNAME",
    "tissue",
    "combo_score",
    "CONC1",
    "CONC2",
    "cellminer_cellline_id",
    "nci_almanac_cellname"
]

assert all(c in MASTER_MODEL.columns for c in KEY_COLS)

def make_row_key(df):
    return pd.util.hash_pandas_object(
        df[KEY_COLS].astype(str),
        index=False
    ).astype(np.uint64)


master_row_keys = make_row_key(MASTER_MODEL)

assert len(master_row_keys) == 294073
assert master_row_keys.nunique() == 294073

print("\nMASTER ROW KEYS")
print("Rows:", len(master_row_keys))
print("Unique:", master_row_keys.nunique())
print("PASS — MASTER rows uniquely identified")


# ============================================================
# 4. LOAD EXISTING SPLITS
# ============================================================

SPLITS = {
    "RANDOM": {
        "path": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/random"
    },
    "COLD_COMBINATION": {
        "path": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_combination"
    },
    "COLD_CELL": {
        "path": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/notebooks/splits/cold_cell"
    },
    "COLD_DRUG": {
        "path": "/Users/anoushka/TrustSyn/splits/cold_drug"
    }
}

split_data = {}

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("LOADING EXISTING SPLITS")
print("=" * 70)

for split_name, info in SPLITS.items():

    path = info["path"]

    assert os.path.exists(path), (
        f"{split_name}: directory not found:\n{path}"
    )

    train_path = os.path.join(path, "train.csv")
    val_path = os.path.join(path, "val.csv")
    test_path = os.path.join(path, "test.csv")

    assert os.path.exists(train_path)
    assert os.path.exists(val_path)
    assert os.path.exists(test_path)

    train_df = pd.read_csv(train_path)
    val_df = pd.read_csv(val_path)
    test_df = pd.read_csv(test_path)

    split_data[split_name] = {

    }

        f"val={val_df.shape}, "
        f"test={test_df.shape}"
    )


# ============================================================
# 5. FUNCTION TO MAP SPLIT ROWS → MASTER ROW INDICES
# ============================================================

def get_master_indices(split_df, split_name, subset_name):

    split_keys = make_row_key(split_df)

    master_key_to_index = pd.Series(
        np.arange(len(master_row_keys)),
        index=master_row_keys
    )

    missing = ~split_keys.isin(master_key_to_index.index)

    assert not missing.any(), (
        f"{split_name} {subset_name}: "
        f"{missing.sum()} rows not found in MASTER_MODEL."
    )

    indices = (
        split_keys
        .map(master_key_to_index)
        .to_numpy(dtype=np.int64)
    )

    assert len(indices) == len(split_df)

    return indices


# ============================================================
# 6. BUILD TRAIN / VAL / TEST MATRICES
# ============================================================

def build_split_matrices(split_name):

    data = split_data[split_name]

    train_idx = get_master_indices(
        data["train"],
        split_name,
        "TRAIN"
    )

    val_idx = get_master_indices(
        data["val"],
        split_name,
        "VAL"
    )

    test_idx = get_master_indices(
        data["test"],
        split_name,
        "TEST"
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Check no row overlap
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    assert len(set(train_idx) & set(val_idx)) == 0
    assert len(set(train_idx) & set(test_idx)) == 0
    assert len(set(val_idx) & set(test_idx)) == 0

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Cold Drug is intentionally a subset of MASTER.
    # Other splits must cover all MASTER rows.
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if split_name != "COLD_DRUG":

        combined = np.concatenate([
            train_idx,
            val_idx,
            test_idx
        ])

        assert len(combined) == 294073
        assert len(np.unique(combined)) == 294073

    else:

        combined = np.concatenate([
            train_idx,
            val_idx,
            test_idx
        ])

        assert len(np.unique(combined)) == len(combined)

        print(
            "\nCOLD_DRUG:",
            len(combined),
            "rows used for strict within-group evaluation"
        )

        print(
            "Excluded cross-group rows:",
            294073 - len(combined)
        )

    return {
        "train_idx": train_idx,
        "val_idx": val_idx,
        "test_idx": test_idx
    }


indices = {}

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("BUILDING SPLIT INDICES")
print("=" * 70)

for split_name in SPLITS:

    indices[split_name] = build_split_matrices(
        split_name
    )

    print(
        f"{split_name}: "
        f"{len(indices[split_name]['train_idx'])} train / "
        f"{len(indices[split_name]['val_idx'])} val / "
        f"{len(indices[split_name]['test_idx'])} test"
    )

print("\nPASS — all split indices validated")


# ============================================================
# 7. CATBOOST CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================
#
# This is a BASELINE.
# We are deliberately NOT doing Optuna yet.
# ============================================================

CATBOOST_PARAMS = {
    "loss_function": "RMSE",
    "eval_metric": "RMSE",

    "iterations": 500,

    "learning_rate": 0.05,
    "depth": 8,

    "l2_leaf_reg": 3,

    "random_seed": 42,

    "verbose": 100,

    "allow_writing_files": False
}


# ============================================================
# 8. METRICS
# ============================================================

def calculate_metrics(y_true, y_pred):

    rmse = np.sqrt(
        mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred)
    )

    mae = mean_absolute_error(
        y_true,
        y_pred
    )

    r2 = r2_score(
        y_true,
        y_pred
    )

    if (
        np.std(y_true) == 0
        or np.std(y_pred) == 0
    ):
        pearson = np.nan
    else:
        pearson = pearsonr(
            y_true,
            y_pred
        )[0]

    return {
        "RMSE": rmse,
        "MAE": mae,
        "R2": r2,
        "Pearson": pearson
    }


# ============================================================
# 9. TRAIN ONE BASELINE PER SPLIT
# ============================================================

baseline_models = {}
baseline_results = {}

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("TRAINING CATBOOST BASELINES")
print("=" * 70)

for split_name in SPLITS:

    print("\n")
    print("#" * 70)
    print(f"TRAINING: {split_name}")
    print("#" * 70)

    idx = indices[split_name]

    train_idx = idx["train_idx"]
    val_idx = idx["val_idx"]
    test_idx = idx["test_idx"]

    X_train = X_np[train_idx]
    y_train = y_np[train_idx]

    X_val = X_np[val_idx]
    y_val = y_np[val_idx]

    X_test = X_np[test_idx]
    y_test = y_np[test_idx]

    print("\nMatrix sizes:")
    print("X_train:", X_train.shape)
    print("y_train:", y_train.shape)
    print("X_val  :", X_val.shape)
    print("y_val  :", y_val.shape)
    print("X_test :", X_test.shape)
    print("y_test :", y_test.shape)

    assert np.isfinite(X_train).all()
    assert np.isfinite(X_val).all()
    assert np.isfinite(X_test).all()

    assert np.isfinite(y_train).all()
    assert np.isfinite(y_val).all()
    assert np.isfinite(y_test).all()

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # MODEL
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    model = CatBoostRegressor(
        **CATBOOST_PARAMS
    )

    model.fit(
        X_train,
        y_train,
        eval_set=(X_val, y_val),
        use_best_model=True
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # PREDICTIONS
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    train_pred = model.predict(X_train)
    val_pred = model.predict(X_val)
    test_pred = model.predict(X_test)

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # METRICS
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    train_metrics = calculate_metrics(
        y_train,
        train_pred
    )

    val_metrics = calculate_metrics(
        y_val,
        val_pred
    )

    test_metrics = calculate_metrics(
        y_test,
        test_pred
    )

    baseline_models[split_name] = model

    baseline_results[split_name] = {
        "train": train_metrics,
        "val": val_metrics,
        "test": test_metrics,
        "best_iteration": model.get_best_iteration()
    }

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # PRINT
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print("\n" + "-" * 70)
    print(f"{split_name} RESULTS")
    print("-" * 70)

    print(
        f"Best iteration: "
        f"{model.get_best_iteration()}"
    )

    for subset_name, metrics in [
        ("TRAIN", train_metrics),
        ("VAL", val_metrics),
        ("TEST", test_metrics)
    ]:

        print(
            f"{subset_name:6s} | "
            f"RMSE: {metrics['RMSE']:.4f} | "
            f"MAE: {metrics['MAE']:.4f} | "
            f"R2: {metrics['R2']:.4f} | "
            f"Pearson: {metrics['Pearson']:.4f}"
        )


# ============================================================
# 10. FINAL RESULTS TABLE
# ============================================================

rows = []

for split_name, result in baseline_results.items():

    for subset_name in ["train", "val", "test"]:

        metrics = result[subset_name]

        rows.append({
            "Split": split_name,
            "Subset": subset_name.upper(),
            "RMSE": metrics["RMSE"],
            "MAE": metrics["MAE"],
            "R2": metrics["R2"],
            "Pearson": metrics["Pearson"],
            "Best_Iteration": result["best_iteration"]
        })

baseline_results_df = pd.DataFrame(rows)


print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("TRUSTSYN CATBOOST BASELINE — FINAL RESULTS")
print("=" * 70)

print(
    baseline_results_df.to_string(
        index=False,
        float_format=lambda x: f"{x:.4f}"
    )
)

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("BASELINE TRAINING COMPLETE")
print("=" * 70)

print("\nModels in memory:")
for name in baseline_models:
    print(
        f"{name}: "
        f"CatBoostRegressor"
    )

print("\nResults object:")
print(
    "baseline_results_df:",
    baseline_results_df.shape
)

print("\nPASS — BASELINE MODELS TRAINED")

import pandas as pd

from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error, r2_score
from scipy.stats import pearsonr

# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# 3. CHECK / REBUILD MASTER_MODEL, X, y

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("CHECKING MODEL OBJECTS")
print("=" * 70)

objects_available = all(
    obj in globals()
    for obj in ["MASTER_MODEL", "X", "y"]

if objects_available:

else:

    print("Model objects not all in memory.")

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # REQUIRED FEATURE PATHS
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    FEATURE_DIR = (

    )

    SIMILARITY_PATH = os.path.join(
        DRUG_DIR,
        "drug_pair_similarity_features_104drug_master_aligned_internal_ids_canonical_pairs.csv"
    )

    TARGET_PATH = os.path.join(
        DRUG_DIR,
        "drug_pair_target_features_104drug_master_aligned_internal_ids_canonical_pairs.csv"
    )

    CELLMINER_PCA_PATH = os.path.join(
        FEATURE_DIR,
        "cellminer_features",
        "cellminer_pca_50_components.csv"
    )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # FIND CELLMINER PCA IF PATH NAME DIFFERS
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if not os.path.exists(CELLMINER_PCA_PATH):

        possible_pca_files = []

        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(FEATURE_DIR):

            for file in files:

                lower = file.lower()

                if (
                    "pca" in lower
                    and "cellminer" in lower
                    and file.endswith(".csv")
                ):
                    possible_pca_files.append(
                        os.path.join(root, file)
                    )

        if len(possible_pca_files) == 1:

            CELLMINER_PCA_PATH = possible_pca_files[0]

        elif len(possible_pca_files) > 1:

            print("\nCandidate CellMiner PCA files:")

            for p in possible_pca_files:
                print(p)

            raise RuntimeError(
                "More than one CellMiner PCA file found. "
                "Use the already validated PCA file explicitly."
            )

        else:

            raise FileNotFoundError(
                "Validated CellMiner PCA file was not found."
            )


    print("\nCellMiner PCA:")
    print(CELLMINER_PCA_PATH)


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # LOAD DRUG FEATURES
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print("\nLoading drug feature matrices...")

    string_pair = pd.read_csv(STRING_PATH)
    kegg_pair = pd.read_csv(KEGG_PATH)
    structure_pair = pd.read_csv(STRUCTURE_PATH)
    similarity_pair = pd.read_csv(SIMILARITY_PATH)
    target_pair = pd.read_csv(TARGET_PATH)

    print("STRING:", string_pair.shape)
    print("KEGG:", kegg_pair.shape)
    print("STRUCTURE:", structure_pair.shape)
    print("SIMILARITY:", similarity_pair.shape)
    print("TARGET:", target_pair.shape)


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # COMMON PAIR KEY
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    def make_pair_key(a, b):

        a = int(float(a))
        b = int(float(b))

        lo = min(a, b)
        hi = max(a, b)

        return f"{lo}_{hi}"


    MASTER_PAIRS = (
        MASTER[["drug_A", "drug_B"]]
        .drop_duplicates()
        .copy()
    )

    MASTER_PAIRS["PAIR_KEY"] = [
        make_pair_key(a, b)
        for a, b in zip(
            MASTER_PAIRS["drug_A"],
            MASTER_PAIRS["drug_B"]
        )
    ]

    assert len(MASTER_PAIRS) == 5143
    assert MASTER_PAIRS["PAIR_KEY"].nunique() == 5143


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # NORMALIZE PAIR FEATURES
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    def normalize_pair_table(
        df,
        name,
        feature_columns
    ):

        df = df.copy()

        # Existing PAIR_KEY
        if "PAIR_KEY" not in df.columns:

            if "drug_A" in df.columns:

                a_col = "drug_A"
                b_col = "drug_B"

            elif (
                "drug_A_id" in df.columns
                and "drug_B_id" in df.columns
            ):

                a_col = "drug_A_id"
                b_col = "drug_B_id"

            else:

                raise ValueError(
                    f"{name}: cannot identify pair columns."
                )

            df["PAIR_KEY"] = [
                make_pair_key(a, b)
                for a, b in zip(
                    df[a_col],
                    df[b_col]
                )
            ]

        # Keep only pair key + requested features
        keep = ["PAIR_KEY"] + feature_columns

        missing = [
            c for c in keep
            if c not in df.columns
        ]

        assert not missing, (
            f"{name}: missing columns {missing}"
        )

        df = df[keep].copy()

        # Check uniqueness
        duplicates = df["PAIR_KEY"].duplicated().sum()

        assert duplicates == 0, (
            f"{name}: {duplicates} duplicate pair keys."
        )

        # Check coverage
        master_keys = set(
            MASTER_PAIRS["PAIR_KEY"]
        )

        feature_keys = set(
            df["PAIR_KEY"]
        )

        missing_pairs = master_keys - feature_keys
        extra_pairs = feature_keys - master_keys

        assert len(missing_pairs) == 0, (
            f"{name}: missing {len(missing_pairs)} MASTER pairs."
        )

        assert len(extra_pairs) == 0, (
            f"{name}: {len(extra_pairs)} extra pairs."
        )

        return df


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # PREPARE EACH FEATURE TABLE
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    string_pair = normalize_pair_table(
        string_pair,
        "STRING",
        [
            "STRING_distance",
            "STRING_available"
        ]
    )

    kegg_pair = normalize_pair_table(
        kegg_pair,
        "KEGG",

            "KEGG_overlap"
        ]
    )

    structure_pair = normalize_pair_table(

    )

    similarity_pair = normalize_pair_table(

        "SIMILARITY",
        [
            "tanimoto_similarity"
        ]
    )

    target_pair = normalize_pair_table(
        target_pair,
        "TARGET",
        [
            "target_count_A",

            "shared_target_count",

            "has_shared_target"
        ]
    )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # BUILD 14-FEATURE DRUG MATRIX
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    drug_pair_features = MASTER_PAIRS.copy()

    for feature_df in [
        string_pair,
        kegg_pair,
        structure_pair,
        similarity_pair,
        target_pair
    ]:

        drug_pair_features = drug_pair_features.merge(

            on="PAIR_KEY",
            how="left",
            validate="one_to_one"
        )


    DRUG_FEATURE_COLS = [
        "STRING_distance",
        "STRING_available",
        "KEGG_overlap",
        "Tanimoto_similarity",
        "Tanimoto_distance",
        "tanimoto_similarity",
        "target_count_A",
        "target_count_B",
        "shared_target_count",
        "union_target_count",
        "target_jaccard",
        "target_overlap_A",
        "target_overlap_B",
        "has_shared_target"
    ]

    assert len(DRUG_FEATURE_COLS) == 14

    # STRING unavailable = distance unavailable
    if (
        "STRING_available" in drug_pair_features.columns
        and "STRING_distance" in drug_pair_features.columns
    ):

        unavailable = (
            drug_pair_features["STRING_available"] == 0
        )

        drug_pair_features.loc[

        ] = 0.0

    assert (

        .isna()
        .sum()

        == 0
    )

    assert np.isfinite(
        drug_pair_features[DRUG_FEATURE_COLS]

    print(

    )


    # --------------------------------------------------------

    master_with_key = MASTER.copy()

    master_with_key["PAIR_KEY"] = [

            master_with_key["drug_A"],
            master_with_key["drug_B"]
        )
    ]

    model_table = master_with_key.merge(
        drug_pair_features[
            ["PAIR_KEY"] + DRUG_FEATURE_COLS
        ],
        on="PAIR_KEY",
        how="left",
        validate="many_to_one"
    )

    assert len(model_table) == 294073


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # LOAD CELLMINER PCA
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    cellminer_pca = pd.read_csv(
        CELLMINER_PCA_PATH
    )

    print(
        "\nCellMiner PCA:",
        cellminer_pca.shape
    )

    assert len(cellminer_pca) == 59

    assert "CELLNAME" in cellminer_pca.columns

    PCA_COLS = [
        c
        for c in cellminer_pca.columns
        if c != "CELLNAME"
    ]

    assert len(PCA_COLS) == 50


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # MERGE CELLMINER PCA
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    model_table = model_table.merge(
        cellminer_pca,
        on="CELLNAME",
        how="left",
        validate="many_to_one"
    )

    assert len(model_table) == 294073

    PCA_VALUES = model_table[PCA_COLS].to_numpy(
        dtype=float
    )

    assert np.isfinite(PCA_VALUES).all()


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # FINAL MODEL MATRIX
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    FEATURE_COLS = (
        DRUG_FEATURE_COLS
        + PCA_COLS
    )

    assert len(FEATURE_COLS) == 64

    MASTER_MODEL = model_table.copy()

    X = MASTER_MODEL[FEATURE_COLS].to_numpy(
        dtype=np.float64
    )

    y = MASTER_MODEL["combo_score"].to_numpy(
        dtype=np.float64
    )

    assert X.shape == (294073, 64)
    assert y.shape == (294073,)

    assert np.isfinite(X).all()
    assert np.isfinite(y).all()

    print("\nPASS — MODEL MATRIX REBUILT")
    print("MASTER_MODEL:", MASTER_MODEL.shape)
    print("X:", X.shape)
    print("y:", y.shape)

    del model_table
    del drug_pair_features
    gc.collect()
